links.comparator_used: Baseline without external evidence (model parametric knowledge alone)
links.effect: No numbers in the abstract. Web-retrieved English evidence was most beneficial for high-resource languages. For low-resource languages, combined English and target-language retrieval gave accuracy comparable to high-resource languages. External knowledge did not improve performance systematically.
links.quote: These findings challenge the assumption that external knowledge systematically improves performance and reveal that effective strategies depend on both the source of language resources and on model scale.

links.comparator_used: Web-retrieved content (open web) versus curated specialized medical repositories such as PubMed
links.outcome: Multilingual medical QA accuracy by evidence source
links.effect: No numbers in the abstract. Web-retrieved English data was most beneficial for high-resource languages, while curated sources such as PubMed were described as limited.
links.tradeoff: Curated sources such as PubMed provide authoritative expert knowledge but lack adequate multilingual coverage.
links.quote: When incorporating external knowledge, web-retrieved data in English proves most beneficial for high-resource languages.
